question: When all nine pixel-cycle combinations fail, does a frozen DINOv2 object-plus-context prototype rank every consumed PV28 query view above both cross-family door/doorframe controls?

predecessor.single_change: Replace pixel-cycle transport with a frozen instance-level object-plus-context descriptor; keep the three reference views, three positive query views, and two cross-family negative queries fixed.

descriptor.feature: Concatenate separately L2-normalized DINOv2 CLS tokens from the exact frozen bbox and a 1.5x clipped context crop, then L2-normalize the concatenation.
descriptor.memory: Mean the three L2-normalized reference descriptors and L2-normalize once.
descriptor.score: Cosine similarity to the frozen three-view prototype.

evaluation.decision_gate: All six positive-versus-negative score comparisons must be strictly ordered correctly; no posthoc absolute threshold or margin is fitted.
evaluation.negative_authority: The two queries come from another physical scan family and cannot contain exact PV28, but they do not test a same-scene sibling.

literature_motivation.use: Summarize several viewpoint-varying object observations and retain surrounding context for instance re-identification.
Move from brittle pixel correspondence to domain-general instance association.

literature_motivation.source: Towards Global Localization Using Multi-Modal Object-Instance Re-Identification
literature_motivation.use: Treat object instances as reusable landmarks rather than only geometric correspondences.

forbidden_after_freeze: change crop scales, feature layer, memory aggregation, images, model or ranking gate
fit an absolute threshold or margin from these five query scores
add or remove a view after seeing descriptor similarity
claim consumed cross-family ranking as fresh or same-scene confirmation
claim_boundary: This consumed Development test can establish only whether a fixed object-plus-context representation contains cross-family-separable PV28 signal under privileged target boxes. It cannot establish same-scene sibling rejection, open-set calibration, raw-camera initial binding, named entrance, ownership, access, traversability, waypoint, arrival, handoff, deployment, benefit, reliability or safety.
